newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa banks borrow foreign exchange - paper.
newsitem.headline: South Africa banks borrow foreign exchange - paper.

text.p: South African banks have borrowed foreign exchange to alleviate the cash crunch, making the money market shortage fall about one billion rand and fuelling bullish sentiment in the bond market, Business Day newspaper reported on Tuesday.
However, money market interest rates failed to respond to the slightly more liquid conditions and bankers warned that an increase in prime rate looked unavoidable.
They said they would have raised their rates by now if they did not fear the political fallout, the paper said.
First National Bank Holdings Ltd treasurer Peter Carroll said on Monday bank margins were in worse shape than they had been when the banks raised rates in May.
"The question is how long will the banks be able to grin and bear it," he said.
Even if the central bank facilitated access to liquid assets, it would not alleviate the pressure in the market.
He said banks would like to see a higher prime overdraft rate. The question was who would move first.

In May, when Standard Bank Investment Corp Ltd triggered a hike in the prime overdraft rate to 20.5 percent, the public outcry was so intense that the banks were put off acting without Reserve Bank approval.
